minutes.headline: Stormwater Task Force met with a quorum only after a late arrival, took no budget action, and set goals and a regulatory workshop.
minutes.summary: The task force nearly lost its quorum, then approved two sets of minutes with Paula joining late. Members discussed adding two new members, the website, complaint tracking, stormwater permit gaps for small projects, catch basin cleaning, grants and a possible stormwater enterprise fund. No budget decisions were made; the task force asked DPW for stormwater spending history and the consultant's scope of work.

budget_items.topic: Revolving fund for stormwater cost recovery
budget_items.what_was_said: Chair asked whether money recouped from developers could go to a stormwater fund; the finance officer said a revolving fund needs a specific purpose and Town Meeting action.

budget_items.topic: Sewer-style stormwater enterprise fund / utility fee
budget_items.what_was_said: Data collection on drains is meant to build the case for a self-supporting enterprise fund or utility fee; members said the need must be established first.
Members discussed 319 and MVP grants and agreed a specific project and cost must be identified first; Paula will compile a list of stormwater grants.

The DPW head said there is a stormwater line mainly for MS4 consultant compliance and a smaller drainage line, with catch basin cleaning in the highway budget; he will estimate stormwater costs across the budget.
An accounting of prior stormwater work was circulated that day, tied to a planned capital amount.

budget_items.topic: Staffing and consultant for stormwater data
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed lacking staff to analyse data and outsourcing to consultants while keeping data ownership for the town.

DPW head to provide past stormwater line item spending and an estimate of stormwater costs across the budget.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force took no budget action; it set goals, a regulatory workshop and requests for DPW spending history.
The DPW head is to provide past stormwater line-item spending and an estimate of stormwater costs across the budget.
Members discussed a stormwater enterprise fund or utility fee and agreed the need must be established first, before any fund is proposed.
The finance officer said a revolving fund for money recouped from developers needs a specific purpose and Town Meeting action.
The meeting opened short of a quorum, which was reached when Paula joined late, and the task force then approved two sets of minutes.

why_it_matters: A stormwater enterprise fund or utility fee would be a new charge on property owners, and any revolving fund would need a Town Meeting vote, so residents may be asked to vote on both later.
Stormwater costs are currently spread across a consulting line, a drainage line and the highway budget, so the DPW estimate is the first step toward seeing the whole cost in one place.
